info_1.title: THE REFERENCE POINT
info_1.description: The ASD Volo Libero Montegrappa was founded in 1979 by a group of friends and pilots, with the aim of promoting free flight around Borso Del Grappa, an area that over the years has established itself as the undisputed destination for thousands of Italian and foreign pilots. Since the 1970s, with the first hang gliders, and then from the late 1980s with paragliding, Borso del Grappa has seen many pilots born and helped them grow in this sport thanks to the special aerological characteristics of the area, its wide take-offs easily accessible, and the almost total absence of strong winds. Perfect characteristics both for beginners and for more experienced pilots who intend to undertake cross-country flights and competitions.

news.title: WHAT'S NEW FOR {NEXT_YEAR}
news.description:
Thanks to an exclusive collaboration agreement reserved for members of Club Volo Libero Montegrappa, a promotion is available for purchasing the annual Flycard at a discounted price of 10€. The Flycard is not included in the membership fee.



How it works:

From January 1st to March 1st, upon completing your Club registration, you will receive a promotional code to use for purchasing the Flycard at the promotional price reserved for members.

The code is personal and unique, can be used only once, and is not transferable to third parties. The code will be sent via email upon payment completion and will always remain available in your reserved area on the website.

important.title: ATTENTION!
important.description:
Membership to Club Volo Libero Montegrappa does not automatically grant immediate right to use the promotion. It is therefore recommended to purchase the Flycard several days in advance of the expected date of use.

For purchase conditions and regulations, please refer to the Vivere il Grappa Consortium website https://flycard.vivereilgrappa.it/rules.



⚠️ For foreign pilots without an Italian Tax Code: to request membership to Club Volo Libero Montegrappa and take advantage of the Flycard promotion, it is necessary to send a request via email to info@vololiberomontegrappa.it.

XcMontegrappaPage.intro:
This initiative is organized and promoted by the Club Volo Libero Montegrappa.

It is not a competition, but a personal challenge that recognizes each pilot's commitment and ability to reach cross-country flying goals.

The routes are based in the Monte Grappa flying area, with takeoff and landing within the designated zones.

Each pilot can freely choose when to fly throughout the season: each season starts on October 1 and ends on September 30 of the following year.

objectives.title: OBJECTIVES
objectives.lead: The XC Montegrappa certificate was created to:
items: Promote and spread free flight practice in paragliding and hang gliding through predefined routes in the Veneto foothills, with takeoff points on Monte Grappa.
Encourage pilots to improve their experience, foster knowledge sharing, and explore nearby flying areas.
Help less experienced pilots approach cross-country flying through progressive route levels.

howItWorks.title: HOW IT WORKS
howItWorks.description:
XC Montegrappa has three difficulty levels (Basic, Intermediate, Advanced), each made up of predefined tasks with waypoints to pass.

Each task has a score that reflects its difficulty. To earn the certificate, you must reach the minimum required score for that level by summing points earned from completed tasks.

This means that, for each level, it is not strictly necessary to complete every task: you only need to reach the minimum score.



Attention! Each task can count only toward one specific certificate level. A single flight track that includes multiple tasks is valid for one of them only. Therefore, different tasks cannot all be completed in one single flight session.

levels.title: CERTIFICATE LEVELS
levels.lead: Certificates are divided into three increasing difficulty levels:

basic.title: BASIC CERTIFICATE
basic.details: Ideal for pilots at their first cross-country experiences.

intermediate.title: INTERMEDIATE CERTIFICATE
intermediate.details: Includes crossing the main valleys around Monte Grappa.

advanced.title: ADVANCED CERTIFICATE
advanced.details: Routes with higher difficulty due to distance, flight time, and crossings through multiple valleys and diverse environmental contexts.

whoCan.question: Who can participate?
whoCan.answer: All Italian and international pilots compliant with current national free-flight regulations and local rules can take part in the XC certificate from Grappa.

howMany.question: How many certificates can I earn?
howMany.answer: There is no distinction or limit by wing category. Each pilot can enroll and complete one or more levels, and can therefore earn all three certificates: basic, intermediate, and advanced.

whenFly.question: When can flights be made?
whenFly.answer: Flights made from October 1st to September 30th of the following year are considered. You can fly on any day of the week, weather permitting.

whenCollect.question: If I reach the required score, when can I collect my certificate?
whenCollect.answer: In October, during the Volo Libero Montegrappa social dinner, certificates are awarded to pilots who achieved the XC certificate from Grappa.

prizes.question: Are there prizes?
prizes.answer: The XC certificate from Grappa is not a competitive event and has no ranking for specific prizes. However, during the social dinner, prizes are drawn among all pilots who achieved the certificate at any level. Special recognitions are granted to pilots who complete multiple certificates in the same season. Drawn prizes are awarded only to pilots present.

ClubPage.intro:
ASD Volo Libero Montegrappa was founded in 1979 by a group of friends and pilots with the aim of promoting free flight around Borso Del Grappa, an area that over the years has established itself as the undisputed destination for thousands of Italian and foreign pilots.



Since the 1970s, with the first hang gliders, and then from the late 1980s with paragliding, Borso del Grappa has seen many pilots born and helped them grow in this sport thanks to the special aerological characteristics of the area, its wide and easily accessible take-offs, and the almost total absence of strong winds. Perfect characteristics both for beginners and for more experienced pilots who want to tackle cross-country flights and competitions.

ClubPage.history_intro:
The history of Volo Libero Monte Grappa begins in the seventies, when people flew where and how they could, self-taught… you bought a hang glider and took off! Years of experimentation, recklessness, pioneering years when flights, though short, were certainly full of excitement: "Take-off Barricata. 4 minutes of flight. Excellent glide" is written in the first logbook of one of the founding members! Then came the first paragliders in the eighties, and the club grew exponentially: pilots increased, schools were born and the facilities we still use today, and in 1982 the first International Free Flight Meeting (later to become Trofeo Montegrappa).

From the 90s to today is a short step, but studded with events, new pilots, new groups that continue, 40 years later, to cultivate and promote the same passion for flight that had inspired the founders!

origins.title: THE EARLY DAYS
origins.body:
The very first Italian hang glider pilots, led by Alfio Caronti, began activities on Lake Como towed by a motorboat, but soon the virus spread like wildfire throughout the Alpine arc and obviously also reached the Grappa. The sacred mountain of the homeland had already been exploited for a "free flight" even in the first post-war period!!! It was 1933 when Aldo Bellò, a native of Solagna, took off with a glider launched by elastic near the summit of Grappa.



40 years later, technology had finally made flying "simpler". The first to take advantage of this in the area was Gaetano Gioppo who initially flew mainly from the "Barricata" on Costo di Asiago. Shortly afterwards, Norberto Savio, Gianni Menegotto and Flavio Ceccato followed him into the air, while the first to return to Grappa after Bellò was probably Gigi Caron. Unfortunately dates and places in this phase are confused



People flew where and how they could, self-taught: you bought a hang glider and took off. Menegotto for example had made his first mountain flights on skis. He had attached a parachuting harness to the hang glider and obviously nobody had told him anything about the attachment height, so he flew calmly with the bar in front of his nose, standing up. All was well until he went around Asiago to try without skis. There was wind and he didn't think he'd have to run so much, but when he started running he realized it took more effort… unfortunately he tripped. The hang glider carried a bit and this spared him damage. He just dragged on his belly down the hillside… 300 metres of meadow… freshly fertilized!! After three days of showers and three nights sleeping in the garage he contacted Gioppo to get lessons. That's how he discovered among other things that on landing the hang glider had to be stalled by pushing on the uprights. Before that he just let go of everything and waited for the thud, or aimed for a hedge. Not for nothing does he hold the record for broken uprights: 4 in a single flight (two on take-off and two later, on landing). 240 thousand lire at the time.



The first hang gliders had a very closed nose, a huge tunnel on the wings and the fabric problem: in case of a stall they dropped the nose and goodnight. That's how Ivano, to avoid stalling, came down so fast he lost the battens in flight. His "instructor" after landing told him "You have to fly again right away" so they bent some electrical conduit to remake the battens and before evening he made his second flight. Of course these primordial hang gliders had a great advantage: you could land even in tight spots, like vegetable gardens and even terraces and windowsills…



Those were years of trials and experiments; calling them pioneering is an understatement.

It was like landing on an unknown planet and having to found a civil society from scratch. In those years we saw biplane hang gliders, hang gliders with cockpits, hang gliders self-built at home (with related demolition of the garage door to get them out). There is also documented the case of a certain Magagnini who "took off" tied to hundreds of balloons!!! When he was high enough he cut the bond and started gliding.



Characteristic of those years was also the topographic map. But not to plan cross-country flights, imagine that. It was used to calculate heights and distances between take-off and landing… to be sure of getting there!! Today's efficiency? Far beyond dreams. "Take-off Barricata. 4 minutes of flight. Excellent glide" is written in Gianni Menegotto's first logbook. Then came the first wings with some performance. Just the fact of staying in the air more than three minutes allowed more people to see these madmen and the group expanded. Delta Club Vicenza was born and a year or two later it was the turn of D.C. Bassano which operated in the area until the death of its president, Walter Zulian, which occurred as a result of a hang check failure. It was a hard blow for the 5-6 pilots who were based on Grappa at the time and for about a year activity was practically suspended.



However, the desire to fly was great and so was the desire to share this passion. So from the ashes of Delta club Bassano in 1979 Volo Libero Montegrappa was born. The club was presided over at the beginning by Flavio Cavalli, another one who had a very sui generis baptism of flight: having got the hang glider he had an appointment at take-off with the "instructor" but that day conditions were really good and the instructor felt like flying so, towards evening, after hours of useless waiting, our man picked up and went down… in flight, obviously.



Also from around that year is the official introduction to the area of the concept of "thermal". Before that, everything that wasn't placid gliding was generically labelled as "turbulence" and carefully avoided. It was with the arrival of Silvio Negrizzolo that things changed: he knew thermals well because he came from sailplanes (once he "parked" one under malga Foraoro…) and he spread the "word" among that bunch of hotheads. So began the cross-country flights, an inexhaustible source of adventures and anecdotes: Gigi Caron once lands in Mussolente, with his white hang glider, white beard and white shirt… "Ze rivà i angeli" (the angels have arrived) an old lady dressed in black tells him, coming out of the house with her hands clasped.. More romantic the adventure of Toni Rizzolo, who flew because he was afraid of flying… After a short cross-country he lands around Caltrano and is helped by a kind girl who later became his wife.

eighties.title: THE 80s
eighties.body:
We're in the eighties. The most turbulent phase is behind us. Clubs were born, the Italian Free Flight Federation was born, a specialized magazine came out, "L'aquilone", the helmet was adopted first and then the reserve parachute and, last but not least, the wings now allowed beautiful flights.



Historic was Silvio Negrizzolo's flight in the spring of '81 from Ceresana to Aviano. From that flight and from a somewhat crazy idea of the Volo Libero Montegrappa board of directors the Meeting Montegrappa was born the following year, with races and the attached flying equipment fair which still fills the foothills skies at Easter today. The first gatherings and competitions were beginning and our people thought that spring conditions were an excellent date to organize an event at the foot of Grappa.



Unfortunately accidents and mishaps are not lacking. Ivano Marzotto (Nene), perhaps the most promising pilot of those years, lost his life aboard an ultralight piloted by an Air Force major. Early 80s: Flavio Cavalli breaks a hang glider wing on the Meatte, plummets, throws the reserve which however gets tangled in the structure. It seems there is no escape and instead while falling the wing stump plants itself in the ground and he remains hanging from the keel, 30 cm from the ground. 1983/84 Roberto Scalettari inadvertently takes off under an occluded front (there were no satellites then). He starts climbing sucked up by the cumulus. The hang glider is covered with ice, some cables break. When he sees the sun again the wrist altimeter shows him 5980 m. He lands in the Marostica area: a first communion is being celebrated nearby and they get him properly drunk.



Thanks to the coordination offered by the club the concept of flight safety also slowly begins to gain ground, not accepted and shared by everyone to be honest. Like the time Flavio, at the time still president of the club, confiscated the battens from a pilot to prevent him from flying in the fog. When Flavio left the stubborn one went into the woods, cut some hazel branches and used those for the hang glider…



These are the years when the platform was built, take-offs and landing fields were identified, the first difficult agreements with farmers were made… In 1984 the Campeggia take-off was "born", still used today for hang gliding competitions. That year there had been a lot of snow (it was the only time they even closed the schools in Rosà for snow, I remember it well…). The panettone was unusable. One week before the race there were still no solutions in sight. Then thanks to a series of fortunate circumstances and connections, in the space of 3 (that's three!) days they managed to have the power line of col Campeggia buried and the race started regularly.



From the second half of the eighties the first paragliders also appeared in Grappa… very much glider and not much para given the "distance" at which they fly from the trees: practically zero.



1988: the movement has assumed such relevance that a law is passed to regulate the activity.



Within a few months pilots in activity are officially recognized with a certificate from the Aero Club d'Italia. Immediately afterwards the first schools are born(Manta is from 1989) and "regular" courses begin.

boom.title: THE BOOM YEARS
boom.body:
'90 and '91 are the boom years of paragliding. Schools turn out hundreds of students per year, take-offs and landing fields are crowded with strange but nice people. It's an epochal leap, free flight has never been so popular. However it manages to maintain a sincere atmosphere of a big family.



Volo Libero Montegrappa is once again ahead of the times and in 1992 organized the 1st Paragrappa Trophy. The event was later cancelled due to bad weather but it is on this core that the following year the Triveneto di Parapendio was born, the first Italian regional race circuit. Since then Borso has hosted a stage of the championship every year.



Also from 1993 is the first "Racing Team" complete with a sponsored van to go to competitions. 1995: the club organizes the Italian paragliding championships. For the first time a task over 100 km is assigned. It will be an unforgettable edition, with weather never seen again in August in these parts (or maybe yes… in 2009)



In 1997 Grappa is again the scene of a world first: the flying wedding. Bride and groom, witnesses, priest, altar boys and guests are all in the air and follow the ceremony via radio. There is also a considerable number of journalists and photographers for full media coverage of the event.



Writing them one after the other like this you wouldn't believe it and yet in 1998 here's another brilliant idea that many have copied… In October the club was supposed to host the final of the Italian cup. Unfortunately the weather was really bad for a traditional race. At most you could do a glide.. The stroke of genius was to do multiple glides… A direct elimination race: 5 pilots at a time, whoever arrives first passes the round. It was two thrilling days! The myth of the Halloween Cup was born!

To offer some entertainment for pilots and the public, since it was late October, the inhabitants of Semonzo had thought of setting up the neighborhood gardens with a "Halloween" theme and still today, after ten years of growth of the event, the Halloween gardens attract hundreds of people to the village on the night of October 31.



In 2001 the club then gave a very great proof of cohesion and passion. At the beginning of the year it was learned that the meeting would no longer take place. The race was still in the official calendar but there were only a few months to organize it. A huge heritage of experiences and traditions was at risk and it was not possible to save the entire event. Thanks to the iron will of the board of directors at the time, however, it was still possible to hold the paragliding race and from the following year exhibitors and therefore also hang gliders returned. Since then the club has directly managed, with the support of the Consorzio Vivere il Grappa, an event that year after year has resumed growing and remains perhaps the only one in the world to group 100 hang gliders and 130 paragliders in the same race days.



In 2004, again during Trofeo Montegrappa, a stage of the Paragliding World Cup circuit arrives, organized in collaboration with Delta Club Feltre.



We are now in recent times. 2009 edition of Trofeo Montegrappa, once again the club proves to be at the forefront. The "Safly Live Tracking" system on Silent Wing software is experimented for the first time in free flight, to follow competitors live during the competition, like in America's Cup races. It's yet another success, with the screen stormed by dozens of pilots and enthusiasts, glued to the video to follow the competition. The system was later also adopted for the world cup final, but the debut was here!



In 2009 the Italian paragliding championships also return to Borso and the 2009 instructor course is also organized. And the story continues..

story_continues.title: THE STORY CONTINUES
story_continues.body:
What else could we invent? Everything seemed already done a bit like when pilots say "modern wings are the top, how could they ever improve them?" It was indeed hard even just to keep the standards reached!



The Trofeo Expo Montegrappa, also thanks to the commitment of important sponsors such as Infinity Fly, Garden Relais and Alpstation Bassano has grown constantly in quantity and quality of pilots, exhibitors and attendees. It has been as usual a great celebration for lovers of our discipline, also opening up to other sports activities. Unfortunately however in 2014 it suffered a sudden and radical setback. It had never happened since 1979 that the Easter appointment at the foot of Grappa was completely cancelled but this time the overlapping of a series of problems forced us to leave. We will return stronger than before in 2015, you'll see!



Races have always been a strong point of our club and until 2012 it was the Team Gare Montegrappa that kept its name high, composed of some of the strongest pilots in the national panorama. Very rich the palmares of victories and placings among which we remember the title of Italian Champion in 2008 in San Potito Sannitico, and in 2009 right in Borso del Grappa, in 2010 vice Italian champion in Poggio Bustone and in 2011 again Italian champion in Assisi.



The same pilots who win the most important races also made themselves available as tutors for group Cross days, in which each one takes under his "inflatable" wing a couple of "chicks" and helps them grow in cross-country flight.



In subsequent years the baton of the Racing Team is picked up by the Ravana Team, born as a joke from a group of newly certified pilots to challenge each other at the Triveneto, over the years it grows to the point of actually winning the Triveneto, obviously under the aegis of AeC Montegrappa.



And what about the commitment to training and updating? In 2009 our area hosts the instructor course in which about thirty expert pilots participate. The following year, together with Montegrappa Tandem Team, we organize the first national tandem pilot stage. Two days of intense work and comparison among tandem pilots from all over Italy. An appointment we will replicate in autumn 2014.



Meanwhile we try to keep members active even in the winter period. Thanks to collaboration with AlpStation Bassano Montura we organize meetings with some of the strongest pilots in the world: Alex Ploner, multiple hang gliding world champion; Nicole Fedele and Jimmy Pacher, European champions and winners of the paragliding world cup; Michael Nesler, world-renowned designer; Peter Gebhard, competitor just outside the podium at X-Alps 2013.



In 2011, right on the wave of the great success of Red Bull X-Alps, the more local X-Grasp was born. With the motto "Who cheats has a small one" we do a test without instrumentation: walk up, short flight route and return to the Garden again on foot. I don't remember the names of the winners, but we had a lot of fun.



Obviously the pilot doesn't live by conferences alone and here are the very popular mountain hut parties and the flying camp (party evening with night in a tent and morning flight). Another classic, skipped this year due to problems with the Camol field, is the trial day organized with ASD Manta, attended by dozens and dozens of curious people who want to try and which has become a party for all the pilots who help out and bring friends and relatives. Although the doubt is that they come mainly for Franco's minestrone… Also grown over time is the collaboration with the Manta school itself which, in parallel with Montegrappa Tandem Team, completes the journey of an aspiring pilot: the team infects them with the flying bug, the school cures them and the club… keeps them healthy and flying!! 🙂



Another nice collaboration was born with the San Floriano flying group, who are always members of AeC Montegrappa on the road. Every year at the end of summer here too a party is organized that always becomes big (in 2014 there was even a tap for beer).



Not all positive unfortunately the events that have seen us protagonists: in recent years we have also had to fight to preserve the possibility of flying on Grappa. Despite the great influx of tourism and work that flying generates, in our area there are still people who try to make us go away and preserving our spaces is often more difficult than one might think. The Consorzio Turistico Vivere il Grappa in addition to collaborating with us in beautiful occasions also supports us in these battles!



Anyway the beauty of AeC Montegrappa is to continuously regenerate itself, to have new forces eager to invent new ways to share the passion for flying and have fun together. Proof of this, right in 2014, are the first editions of CarnevalVolando in February and Tri-Grasp-Thlon right during the social party (end of season highlight event). Groups and events come and go, meteors or fixed stars depends on fate. But there is always someone ready to pick up the baton and propose new ideas. Dear members: you are our strength, thank you all! …and the story continues!

farewell.title: FLIGHTS, SMILES and A SEE YOU SOON
farewell.body:
Already 5 years have passed and here we are for the 2019 update!



In 2015 Trofeo Montegrappa returns with a grandiose Expo edition at the Conca Verde pools. Unfortunately the difficulties are not over and in subsequent years we had quite a few problems organizing it. To aggravate the situation the relationship with AeCI deteriorated to the point that Montegrappa returned to being ASD Volo libero Montegrappa.

The commitment however was rewarded and in 2019 we had one of the most memorable editions in history, with a task of almost 160 km in the Dolomites.



In 2017 our area also hosted some tasks of the Feltre Paragliding World Championship, a great success of our cousins. Honoring its tradition (we were among the founders) the club has hosted a stage of the Triveneto every year, if not the final. In 2018 we also had a stage of the Dolomiti Superfly. The palmares of our best pilots is enriched with victories and prestigious placings: in 2017 Valentino Baù wins with the Italian national team the Hang Gliding World Championship in Brazil, in 2018 Loris Berta places second at the Italian Paragliding Championship in Poggio Bustone and first at Trofeo Guarnieri in Feltre (British Open). Finally Gianfranco Crestani arrives second at Trofeo Montegrappa 2019 serial class.



As you now know however the club only marginally deals with races, our real target is flying and the fun it can bring. For example in 2017 at the social dinner we had Chiara Dello Iacovo in concert, star of The Voice and Sanremo Giovani. The end of summer party "on the road" in Valle San Floriano becomes more beautiful every year and involves more new friends. The social party is the most popular appointment and the "corn cob award" one of the most coveted.



In these years we have also taken care of the preparation and updating of pilots. The list of this part includes the meeting with Marius Ganthaler who told us about his differently-abled approach to flying. Under the supervision of Montegrappa Tandem Team in autumn 2018 the new tandem pilot stage took place, organized in the setting of the Filippin institutes in Paderno, which saw the participation of 150 pilots from all over Italy. In January 2019 an intriguing and demanding course on weather and cross-country flying held at Garden Relais by Damiano Zanocco.



Also noteworthy is the birth of a new very active group of newly certified pilots. In 2017 the Parazoo were born who in just two years have already given a lot to the club, not least a second party in Valle San Floriano 🙂



In these years after the X-grasp experiment and the more complex and renowned Tri-Grasp-Thlon the love for hike and fly has also grown with us and more and more often on the Grappa trails you meet more or less sweaty pilots equipped with more or less light equipment.



The "struggle" with bureaucracy continues to keep the flying site open and for this we must certainly thank the Consorzio Vivere il Grappa for the help it is giving to the new club board of directors. A very positive symbolic news in this sense: in 2019 for the first time a mayor of Borso (Flavio Dall'Agnol) flew in tandem with paragliding and on landing was very happy! If they are roses they will bloom, we would really need it to finally fix the take-offs in a decent manner.



In the summer of 2019 in collaboration with ASD Manta we celebrated the 40 years of the club and the 30 of the school with a nice party at the pool.



Unfortunately we must conclude the narration of this five-year period with very sad news. In June 2018 in fact our Flavio left us, victim of a flying accident right in the skies of Semonzo. It was a shock but we are certain that now we have one more angel watching over all of us.

stella.description:
Grassy take-off, suitable for paragliders, in the municipality of Borso del Grappa along the Generale Giardino road (SP 140), about 200 m after the 13th hairpin bend.

It works mainly with southerly wind and light easterly and westerly winds.

Parking is scarce, so we strongly recommend using the shuttle service to get here.

tappeti.description:
The main take-off of the area, with a synthetic carpet for paragliders, in the municipality of Borso del Grappa along the Generale Giardino road (SP 140), about 200 m before the 17th hairpin bend where the hang-gliding ramp (Decollo Pedana) is, next to the Puppolo bar and trattoria.

It works mainly with southerly wind and light easterly and westerly winds.

Parking is scarce, so we strongly recommend using the shuttle service to get here.

Beware: an easterly wind can cause turbulence. Lay out your wing only once you are in your harness, so as not to occupy the area for too long.

pedana-delta.description:
Take-off reserved for hang gliders, in the municipality of Borso del Grappa along the Generale Giardino road (SP 140), at the 17th hairpin bend.

It is an iron and wood launch ramp, with an area for rigging the gliders on the grass inside the hairpin.

The area in front of the bar must be kept clear for hang gliders on their way to launch.

Parking is scarce, so we strongly recommend sharing rides or using the shuttle service.
pedana-delta.warning: Taking off with a paraglider from the hang-gliding ramp is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN.

casette.description:
Grassy take-off suitable for paragliders, in the municipality of Borso del Grappa along the Generale Giardino road (SP 140).

About 300 m after the 20th hairpin bend, take the narrow uphill road on the left towards Col Serai. After 100 m, past a small right-hand bend, the take-off is on the left.

It works with westerly wind.

There is no parking, so we strongly recommend using the shuttle service.

Please respect private property and do not leave cars parked along the road.
casette.warning: Taking off towards the east is strictly forbidden: danger of death ☠️

camol.description:
Grassy take-off suitable for paragliders, along the Generale Giardino road (SP 140).

To get there, follow the signs for Cima Grappa and, 800 m after the 21st hairpin bend, park at Baita Camol and walk to the start of trail no. 100 towards Cima Grappa. 400 m along the trail, the wide take-off meadow is recognisable by its windsock. It works mainly with south to south-westerly winds.

panettone.description:
A striking grassy take-off just below Cima Grappa.

Along the Generale Giardino road (SP 140), about 500 m after the 27th hairpin bend, where trail no. 100 crosses the road, there is a small car park. On the right, the windsock of the Panettone take-off stands on top of the hillock.

This very large take-off, facing east to south-east, is suitable for both paragliders and hang gliders.

The west-facing take-off is smaller and suitable for paragliders.

On this second take-off in particular, watch out for some war-time holes hidden in the grass.

campeggia.description:
Along the Cadorna road (SP 148), follow the signs for Cima Grappa up to Campo Solagna. 300 m past the bar and restaurant, take the narrow road on the right following the signs for Col Campeggia. After the second hairpin bend, at a small junction, you reach the Col Campeggia take-off.

It works with south to south-easterly winds and light south to south-westerly winds.

Pay close attention to the wind strength, as the take-off lies in a narrow valley.

In the afternoon there may be lee-side turbulence from the south-west.
campeggia.notice: Take-off intended mainly for event days, not for everyday use. To use it, a request must be sent in advance.

antenne.description:
Grassy take-off suitable for paragliders.

After the seventh hairpin bend along the Cadorna road (SP 148), the take-off, also known as Costa Lunga, is on the left.

Use it with easterly winds.

The car park next to the meadow is small, so we strongly recommend using the shuttle service.

Watch out for the marked turbulence zones.

In the afternoon there may be lee-side turbulence from the south and/or west.

garden.description:
Large landing field in Semonzo, at the Garden Relais hotel, via Casa 22, Borso del Grappa, Treviso.

It is suitable for hang gliders and paragliders, and you can land in all four directions: north, south, west and east.

Take particular care when landing in a strong westerly wind, as the field is then in the lee of the hills and the hotel building. Also watch out for the trees and vineyards around the field, and for the car park along the north side. The landing areas are marked A, B and C in the photo.

If you land outside the field, please move to the packing areas as quickly as possible.

paradiso.description:
The Paradiso landing is in Semonzo, in via Casale Nuovo, at the junction with via Giovanni da Semonzo.

It is for paragliders only. Take particular care with the power and telephone lines south of the field, and with the vineyards and trees around it. The landing areas are marked A and B in the photo.

Please respect private property and, if you land outside the field, leave without causing damage.

The landing has a large car park, toilets, and places to eat and drink a few hundred metres away, within walking distance.
